description: Identify the book of the Bible a passage comes from. Passages are quoted from the New American Bible, revised edition. The player types the book name; acceptedAnswers carries the ordinary variants (numbered-book spellings, common short forms).

items.passage: In the beginning, when God created the heavens and the earth—and the earth was without form or shape, with darkness over the abyss and a mighty wind sweeping over the waters—
items.explanation: The opening of Genesis: God creates an ordered cosmos out of nothing, freely and by His word.

items.passage: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. You shall not have other gods beside me.
items.explanation: The first of the Ten Commandments, given at Sinai after the deliverance from Egypt.

items.passage: The LORD is my shepherd; there is nothing I lack. In green pastures he makes me lie down; to still waters he leads me; he restores my soul.
items.explanation: Psalm 23, the shepherd psalm, trusts God's provision and guidance through every danger.

items.passage: For a child is born to us, a son is given to us; upon his shoulder dominion rests. They name him Wonderful Counselor, God-Hero, Father-Forever, Prince of Peace.
items.explanation: Isaiah's prophecy of the messianic king, read by the Church at Christmas.

items.passage: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, on your own intelligence do not rely; in all your ways be mindful of him, and he will make straight your paths.
items.explanation: A proverb on the wisdom of entrusting one's whole life to God rather than to one's own cleverness.

items.passage: There is an appointed time for everything, and a time for every affair under the heavens. A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot the plant.
items.explanation: Qoheleth reflects on the seasons of human life, all of them held within God's providence.

items.passage: Naked I came forth from my mother's womb, and naked shall I go back again. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD!
items.explanation: Job's response to catastrophic loss, holding to worship without cursing God.

items.passage: But the LORD sent a large fish to swallow Jonah, and he remained in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
items.explanation: Jonah's three days in the fish, which the Lord names as a sign of His own three days in the tomb.

items.passage: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are they who mourn, for they will be comforted.
items.explanation: The opening of the Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount.

items.passage: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things came to be through him.
items.explanation: The prologue of John's Gospel, proclaiming the eternity and divinity of the Word made flesh.

items.passage: Do not be afraid; for behold, I proclaim to you good news of great joy that will be for all the people. For today in the city of David a savior has been born for you who is Messiah and Lord.
items.explanation: The angel's announcement to the shepherds on the night of the Nativity.

items.passage: When the time for Pentecost was fulfilled, they were all in one place together. And suddenly there came from the sky a noise like a strong driving wind, and it filled the entire house.
items.explanation: The descent of the Holy Spirit on the apostles at Pentecost, the birthday of the Church's mission.

items.passage: We know that all things work for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose.
items.explanation: Paul's assurance that God draws good even out of suffering for those united to Him.

items.passage: If I speak in human and angelic tongues but do not have love, I am a resounding gong or a clashing cymbal. Love is patient, love is kind.
items.explanation: Paul's hymn to charity, the greatest of the theological virtues and the form of all the rest.

items.passage: I have the strength for everything through him who empowers me.
items.explanation: Paul, writing from prison, on the sufficiency of Christ's grace in every circumstance.

items.passage: Faith is the realization of what is hoped for and evidence of things not seen. Because of it the ancients were well attested.
items.explanation: The definition of faith that opens Hebrews' roll-call of the faithful of the old covenant.

items.passage: So also faith of itself, if it does not have works, is dead. Indeed someone might say, “You have faith and I have works.” Demonstrate your faith to me without works, and I will demonstrate my faith to you from my works.
items.explanation: James on the inseparability of living faith and charitable works.

items.passage: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The former heaven and the former earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. I also saw the holy city, a new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God.
items.explanation: John's vision of the consummation of all things, when God will dwell with His people fully and forever.

items.passage: Hear, O Israel! The LORD is our God, the LORD alone! Therefore, you shall love the LORD, your God, with your whole heart, and with your whole being, and with your whole strength.
items.explanation: The Shema, Israel's daily prayer, which the Lord names as the greatest commandment.

items.passage: And the LORD said to Moses: Make a saraph and mount it on a pole, and everyone who has been bitten will look at it and recover. Accordingly Moses made a bronze serpent and mounted it on a pole.
items.explanation: The bronze serpent in the wilderness, which the Lord names as a figure of His own being lifted up on the cross.

items.passage: If it is displeasing to you to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve... As for me and my household, we will serve the LORD.
items.explanation: Joshua's charge to Israel at Shechem after the conquest, calling the people to renew the covenant.

items.passage: Samson called to the LORD and said, “Lord GOD, remember me! Strengthen me only this once... that I may avenge myself on the Philistines for the loss of my two eyes.”
items.explanation: The blinded Samson's last prayer, in which his strength returns and the temple of Dagon falls.

items.passage: So Eli said to Samuel, “Go to sleep, and if you are called, reply, ‘Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.’”
items.explanation: The boy Samuel's call in the night at the sanctuary of Shiloh.

items.passage: Then Nathan said to David: “You are the man! Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I anointed you king of Israel... Why have you despised the LORD and done what is evil in his sight?”
items.explanation: The prophet Nathan confronts David over Bathsheba and Uriah, and David repents.

items.passage: When all the people saw this, they fell prostrate and said, “The LORD is God! The LORD is God!”
items.explanation: The people's response after fire falls from heaven on Elijah's altar on Mount Carmel.

items.passage: So Naaman went down and plunged into the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God. His flesh became again like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
items.explanation: The Syrian commander Naaman is healed of leprosy by obeying the prophet Elisha.

items.passage: Do not be saddened this day, for rejoicing in the LORD is your strength!
items.explanation: Nehemiah and Ezra to the people weeping as the Law is read aloud after the return from exile.

items.passage: “I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand and serve before the Glory of the Lord.” ... they were both terrified and fell to the ground.
items.explanation: The angel Raphael reveals himself after guiding Tobiah and healing the blindness of Tobit.

items.passage: The Lord Almighty thwarted them by the hand of a woman. ... She took hold of the hair of his head... and struck his neck twice with all her might, and cut off his head.
items.explanation: The widow Judith delivers Bethulia by killing the Assyrian general Holofernes.

items.passage: “You accursed fiend, you are depriving us of this present life, but the King of the universe will raise us up to live again forever.”
items.explanation: The second of seven brothers martyred with their mother rather than break the law, professing the resurrection of the body.

items.passage: But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. They seemed, in the view of the foolish, to be dead... but they are in peace.
items.explanation: A meditation on the immortality of the righteous, often read at funerals.

items.passage: All wisdom is from the Lord and remains with him forever. The sand of the seas, the drops of rain, the days of eternity: who can count them?
items.explanation: The opening of Ben Sira's book of practical wisdom for living in the fear of the Lord.

items.passage: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for Love is strong as Death, longing is fierce as Sheol. Its arrows are arrows of fire, flames of the divine.
items.explanation: Love poetry read by the tradition as the love of God for His people and Christ for the Church.

items.passage: The LORD's acts of mercy are not exhausted, his compassion is not spent; they are renewed each morning—great is your faithfulness!
items.explanation: A flash of hope in the middle of the dirge over the ruin of Jerusalem.

items.passage: I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
items.explanation: God's promise, through Ezekiel in exile, of an interior renewal fulfilled in the new covenant.

items.passage: When Israel was a child I loved him, out of Egypt I called my son. ... It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, who took them in my arms.
items.explanation: God's tender complaint over His unfaithful people, using the image of a parent and a wayward child.

items.passage: I hate, I spurn your feasts... But if you offer me burnt offerings, I will not accept them. ... Rather let justice surge like waters, and righteousness like an unfailing stream.
items.explanation: The shepherd-prophet Amos against worship divorced from justice for the poor.

items.passage: You have been told, O mortal, what is good, and what the LORD requires of you: Only to do justice and to love goodness, and to walk humbly with your God.
items.explanation: Micah's summary of true religion, and elsewhere he names Bethlehem as the birthplace of the ruler of Israel.

items.passage: Exult greatly, O daughter Zion! Behold: your king is coming to you, a just savior is he, humble, and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
items.explanation: The prophecy fulfilled on Palm Sunday when the Lord enters Jerusalem.

items.passage: From the rising of the sun to its setting, my name is great among the nations; incense offerings are made to my name everywhere, and a pure offering.
items.explanation: A prophecy the Church reads as pointing to the one pure offering of the Eucharist, made in every place.

items.passage: Then he said to them, “The sabbath was made for man, not man for the sabbath. That is why the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.”
items.explanation: From the shortest and most fast-paced of the Gospels, on the purpose of the Lord's day.

items.passage: I have been crucified with Christ; yet I live, no longer I, but Christ lives in me; insofar as I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God who has loved me and given himself up for me.
items.explanation: Paul on the believer's whole life now hidden in Christ.

items.passage: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. For in him were created all things in heaven and on earth... all things were created through him and for him.
items.explanation: An early hymn on the supremacy of Christ over all creation.

items.passage: I have competed well; I have finished the race; I have kept the faith. From now on the crown of righteousness awaits me.
items.explanation: Paul's words near the end of his life, in what reads as a last testament to a younger co-worker.

items.passage: But you are “a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people of his own, so that you may announce the praises” of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
items.explanation: Peter applies to the baptized the titles once given to Israel at Sinai.

items.passage: Whoever is without love does not know God, for God is love. ... God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God and God in him.
items.explanation: The letter that most directly identifies the very nature of God with love.

items.passage: Beloved... I now feel a need to write to encourage you to contend for the faith that was once for all handed down to the holy ones.
items.explanation: A short, sharp letter urging its readers to hold fast the apostolic faith against those who distort it.
